Weekly Work Report
Period: July 30, 2026 – Aug 06, 2026
Prepared by: Gao Zhen
Total Billable Hours: 20 Hours

1. RNA-seq outlier diagnostics Analysis – Jinlonf Yu (2.5 Hours)
Diagnosed why one animal (J_902) sat apart from its group mates in a 12-sample mouse skeletal-muscle RNA-seq time course, 
Showed the sample is partly a different tissue (7.0% adipose-derived transcriptome vs 0.06–1.60% elsewhere; type IIa fibers 18.4% vs 0.2–7.2%), 
Scored every sample on a treatment signature in units of baseline SD, reproducing the design cleanly (G1 = 22.1, G3 = 15.3, G2 = 6.4, baseline = 0.0) 
and placing J_902 at 6.3 — collected with an effect-present group but transcriptionally at the effect-resolved level. 
Left the two remaining explanations (wrong collection point/label vs genuinely faster resolution),
noting the client's PK data argues against drug clearance. Also quantified that the deviation is moderate (1.5–1.8× normal).

2.WGS reanalysis  — Ellen, knock-in junction sequences (8.5 hours)
Resolved the knock-in junctions to base resolution from read-level alignment evidence for six humanized lines (MTTH ×3, RAGH ×2, CD1A ×1), 
All 12 junction windows per package showing 100.0% identity to the client's targeted-allele reference. 
Supplied the individual reads that span each human/mouse boundary in a single 150 bp read at MAPQ 60, and reported exact coordinates. 
Characterised the designed vector remnants — an 87 bp vector segment containing the residual FRT scar on the 3′ side, plus two retained loxP sites in CD1A — 
and flagged that the CD1A construct is integrated in reverse orientation relative to chr3. 
Carried out the structural confirmation the July 12 report had recommended for MTTH_284, resolving its multi-copy on-target integration as a complex array with both direct and inverted junctions, 
Recommended MTTH_412 and MTTH_524 as the founders to take forward.

3.Sample Registration Form Redesign (9.0 Hours)
Transformed the original fill-in-the-blank sample submission form into a checkbox-driven structured document, 
covering RNAseq/WGS/single-cell/spatial transcriptomics/gene targeting/cell line characterization across all business scenarios.
**Core changes:**
1. **Format overhaul** — Converted open-ended questions into `□` checkbox lists; the client's main task shifted from "typing" to "checking" (□→☑)
2. **Main sheet simplification** — Moved specialized content (Gene Targeting, Cell Line, Humanized System, Other Services, Special Design) to dedicated Sheets 2-7; 
The main sheet now only shows a one-line jump pointer, so general clients aren't overwhelmed by technical jargon
3. **Section restructuring** — merged all sections in one Unbrella strucuture, unified numbering sequence
4. **Visual consistency** — Standardized color scheme across the workbook (required = orange-red, jump pointers = unified purple tone, warnings = amber), condensed loosely-spaced checkbox groups into single compact cells
5. **Usability** — Added a prominent instruction banner at the top of every sheet teaching clients how to type the checkmark character
**Benefits**:
1. **Reduced client time** — Not much writing is needed anymore
2. **Improved client experience** less intellegual and labor burdon for clients 
2. **reduced misunderstanding** — avoid confusion in oral or informal commuinication

Weekly Work Report
Period: July 30, 2026 – Aug 06, 2026
Prepared by: Gao Zhen
Total Billable Hours: 19 Hours

1. RNA-seq Outlier Diagnostics Analysis — Jinlong Yu (2.5 Hours)
Diagnostic Investigation: Investigated an outlier sample (J_902) in a 12-sample mouse skeletal-muscle RNA-seq time course.
Tissue Contamination Identification: Demonstrated that the sample contains partial contamination from a different tissue, 
exhibiting a 7.0% adipose-derived transcriptome (vs. 0.06–1.60% elsewhere) and 18.4% type IIa fibers (vs. 0.2–7.2% elsewhere).
Treatment Signature Scoring: Scored every sample based on a treatment signature in units of baseline SD, which cleanly reproduced 
the experimental design (G1 = 22.1, G3 = 15.3, G2 = 6.4, baseline = 0.0). Sample J_902 scored 6.3, indicating it was collected 
with an effect-present group but transcriptionally matched the effect-resolved level.
Conclusion & Recommendations: Quantified the deviation as moderate (1.5–1.8× normal). 
Narrowed the cause down to either incorrect collection timing/labeling or genuinely faster biological resolution, 
noting that the client's PK data argues against drug clearance.

2. WGS Reanalysis — Ellen, Knock-in Junction Sequences (8.5 Hours)
Junction Resolution: Resolved knock-in junctions to base-pair resolution using read-level alignment evidence for six humanized lines (MTTH ×3, RAGH ×2, CD1A ×1). 
Confirmed that all 12 junction windows per package showed 100.0% identity to the client's targeted-allele reference.
Data Delivery: Supplied individual reads spanning each human/mouse boundary in a single 150 bp read at MAPQ 60, alongside exact coordinates.
Vector Remnant Characterization: Characterized the designed vector remnants, identifying an 87 bp vector segment containing the residual FRT scar on the 3′ side 
and two retained loxP sites in CD1A. Flagged that the CD1A construct is integrated in a reverse orientation relative to chr3.
Structural Confirmation: Performed the structural confirmation recommended in the July 12 report for MTTH_284. Resolved its multi-copy on-target integration as 
a complex array featuring both direct and inverted junctions. Actionable Recommendation: Recommended MTTH_412 and MTTH_524 as the optimal founders to take forward.

3. Sample Registration Form Redesign (8.0 Hours)
Redesigned the original fill-in-the-blank sample submission form into a structured, checkbox-driven document. 
The new form comprehensively covers RNA-seq, WGS, single-cell, spatial transcriptomics, gene targeting, and cell line characterization across all business scenarios.
Core Changes Implemented:
Format Overhaul: Converted open-ended questions into checkbox lists (□), shifting the client's primary task from typing to checking (☑).
Main Sheet Simplification: Moved specialized content (Gene Targeting, Cell Line, Humanized System, Other Services, Special Design) to dedicated Sheets 2–7. 
The main sheet now features a single-line jump pointer, preventing general clients from being overwhelmed by technical jargon.
Section Restructuring: Merged all sections under a single umbrella structure with a unified numbering sequence.
Visual Consistency: Standardized the color scheme across the workbook (Required = orange-red, Jump Pointers = unified purple, Warnings = amber). 
Condensed loosely-spaced checkbox groups into compact, single cells.
Usability Enhancements: Added a prominent instruction banner at the top of every sheet detailing how to type the checkmark character.
Projected Benefits:
Time Efficiency: Significantly reduces the time required for clients to complete submissions.
Enhanced User Experience: Lowers the cognitive and manual burden on clients by replacing open-ended text fields with structured choices.
Increased Accuracy: Minimizes ambiguities, misunderstandings, and data entry errors that commonly arise from informal or written communication.

Weekly Work Report
Period: Aug 13, 2026 - Aug 20, 2026
Prepared by: Gao Zhen
Total Billable Hours: 20 Hours

1. WGS Sequencing Run - Keqiang, Second Batch (2.5 Hours)
Completed the sequencing run and initial data processing for the second batch of samples,
bringing the two-batch dataset to a state where it could be analyzed as a single cohort.

2. Integrative WGS Analysis - Keqiang (12.0 Hours)
Integrative Analysis: Performed a highly complex integrative analysis across the two sequencing batches,
resolving numerous inconsistencies in the sample and reference materials before any conclusion could be drawn.
Integration Assessment: Determined transgene copy number and integration structure for the clones at the targeted
safe-harbour locus, distinguishing clones that carry the complete plasmid including backbone from those carrying
the intended cassette only.
Off-target Screening: Screened the genome for additional integration events. During the pre-delivery audit, the
large majority of the initial candidate list was excluded as PCR-duplicate artefacts rather than genuine events,
and two clones were shown to share base-identical junctions and therefore not to represent independent events.
Host-background Caveat: Documented a host cell line background that inflates the apparent vector signal for certain
elements, with a falsification test showing the excess is constant across a wide copy-number range and is therefore
additive background rather than true integration.
Reporting: All details, evidence and reasoning were provided to the client in the written report and the
accompanying communication.

3. RNA-seq Analysis - Junqiang (3.0 Hours)
Complete Analysis: Performed the end-to-end analysis of a 12-sample, four-group dataset and delivered all six
pairwise comparisons.
Interpretation under an Undisclosed Design: The submission provided no biological meaning for the four groups.
Gene-, cluster- and pathway-level results were therefore reported strictly as measured and discussed with additional
care, explicitly separating what the data show from what cannot be concluded without the experimental design.
Statistical Caveats Documented: Explained why the comparisons with the largest number of differentially expressed
genes return the fewest enriched terms (a property of over-representation testing, not an absence of biology), and
flagged the pathway terms that are driven by mitochondrial-genome-encoded transcripts as compositional rather than
as evidence of pathway induction.

4. Client Service and Internal Communication (2.5 Hours)
Communicated with clients to clarify sample details, experimental designs, sequences used, and cell line and naming
discrepancies.
Answered numerous technical, statistical and methodological inquiries.
Internal discussion and coordination via WeChat.
